disasters.summary: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the northern coast of East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, on 14 August 2026 (15 August local time). At least 68 deaths were reported by 17 August, with more than 130 injured and thousands evacuated. Damage was reported in Sikka, Manggarai, Nagekeo and Ngada. Aftershocks continued, and BMKG warned activity could last 3–4 weeks. The provincial emergency response period was set for 15–28 August.

disasters.title: Sierra Leone: Freetown flash flood
disasters.summary: Flash flooding hit Freetown and the wider Western Area Urban District, Sierra Leone, from 3 August 2026. The IFRC DREF operation runs from 13 August to 31 December 2026. Four deaths are confirmed. About 8,915 people in 1,763 families were affected, and more than 700 houses were flooded, damaged or destroyed. An EU statement of 24 August says the rainy season continues and the risk of further flash flooding and landslides remains high.

disasters.summary: Floods and landslides struck Limbe, Fako Division, South-West Region, Cameroon, on 5 August 2026 after prolonged torrential rain. Three people died and six houses collapsed, according to reports from 7 to 11 August. One family member was injured and taken to hospital. An IFRC DREF operation (MDRCM045) started on 13 August 2026. The latest report found is dated 27 August 2026.

disasters.summary: Wildfires have hit Tunisia since early June 2026, according to sources, and the IFRC timeline lists 25 July as the start. Sixteen governorates were affected, and about 12,000 hectares of forest and farmland were damaged. The Tunisian Red Crescent assessed 41,479 people affected. An IFRC operation runs to 28 February 2027. The latest source is dated 1 September 2026; whether fires were still burning on 22 October was not confirmed.

disasters.title: Kyrgyzstan: Nooken Mudflow
disasters.summary: On 13 July 2026, intense rainfall triggered mudflows across Nooken district, Jalal-Abad region, Kyrgyzstan. Floodwater and mud affected nearly 3,000 people, and no deaths or injuries were reported. Clean-up was under way in early reporting. The latest source, dated 10 September 2026, describes the floods as past and reports €90,000 in EU humanitarian funding for affected households.

Casualties and damage extent were not reported by authorities as of 13 July 2026. No later status was found.
